checks.covers: URLs and URLSearchParams, searchParams and request params that carry a password, secret or API key parameter name
checks.misses: Sensitive values under other parameter names or sent through generic names (token, id, code); URLs built from several parts; session tokens in paths; what a deployed system logs or leaks in URLs; an informational finding that does not block unless the HTML rule applies; request bodies and connection strings written with the same parameter names are reported too

checks.covers: HTML forms with an explicit method=get attribute and a password-type input before the closing form tag
checks.misses: Forms with no method attribute (the separate Review half), script-controlled submission, sensitive fields of other types, dynamically built markup, and what a deployed system logs or leaks.

checks.covers: Points at HTML forms with a password-type input and no method attribute, where browser-default GET can put the password in the query string.
checks.misses: The protection may exist where the rule cannot see it, such as script setting the method or intercepting submission; other sensitive field types, dynamic markup and deployed URL handling are not modeled. This Review prompt never examines the requirement.

entries.why: Sensitive parameter names in URLs and password forms with explicit GET remain partial checks. A form with an omitted method is only a Review prompt, never examination evidence; its actual submission handling needs confirmation.

checks.covers: A model reading the source for code that sends user data or identifiers to analytics, advertising or tracking services
checks.misses: What is actually sent at run time; third-party scripts loaded by tag managers; data classified as sensitive in documents the repository does not hold

entries.why: Whether data counts as sensitive and whether a recipient is untrusted needs reading the code in context, so the review method examines it.

checks.covers: A model reading the source for responses and views that return more of a sensitive value than the function needs, such as a full card or national id number
checks.misses: Data shaped by the database or a serializer in another place; behavior at run time

entries.why: Minimum exposure of sensitive data depends on what each function needs, which no pattern can judge, so the review method reads the code.

checks.covers: A model reading the source for upload handling that stores or forwards files without removing metadata such as location or author fields
checks.misses: Metadata removed by a storage service or proxy; consent kept in the product; files processed outside the repository

entries.why: Metadata handling of uploaded files is visible in the code that processes them but not by pattern, so the review method reads it.

checks.covers: A model reading client code for data of a signed-in user that stays in the DOM or browser storage after the session ends, and for sign-out code that clears it
checks.misses: Server headers set elsewhere; behavior in a real browser; state kept by libraries

entries.why: Clearing client state on sign-out is a property of client flows across files, so the review method reads the code; it concerns browser code only.

checks.covers: Cache-control alerts of the ZAP scan of a running target: re-examine cache-control directives, and storable and cacheable content
checks.misses: Responses on pages ZAP did not reach; whether a response holds sensitive data (ZAP cannot tell); authenticated pages if no authentication header was given

entries.why: No repository check can show the absence of a header; the ZAP alerts listed report responses of a running target that lack anti-caching directives.

checks.covers: LocalStorage and sessionStorage writes whose key names a password, secret, API key, card number or national id
checks.misses: IndexedDB and cookies; sensitive values under other key names or in the value only; session tokens (an allowed exception) are not told apart; what the browser holds in a running application

entries.why: The rule flags localStorage and sessionStorage writes under key names that describe sensitive data; it concerns browser code only.
